scope: New event for this routing and writing study. Inventories are simulated and the learned router sees card slots, not language. Base-model pretraining exposure is unknown.

public.VOTE: At meeting S/PV.9591 on 28 March 2024, the U.S.-submitted draft S/2024/255 received 13 votes in favour, Russia against and China abstaining. Russia's permanent-member negative vote prevented adoption.
public.MANDATE: Draft S/2024/255 proposed extending the Panel of Experts assisting the 1718 Committee until 30 April 2025. It reaffirmed that the Panel should provide credible, independent, fact-based assessments.
public.REPORTING: The draft requested confidential midterm and final reports to the 1718 Committee. The draft's proposed reporting dates and mandate extension did not take effect.
public.SCOPE: The 1718 Committee continued to work and the existing sanctions remained in force after the Panel mandate ended on 30 April 2024.

JAPAN.text: Council President Yamazaki spoke in his national capacity as Japan’s representative. He regretted Russia’s veto and said it forced the Panel of Experts to end operations. After the statement he resumed the presidency.
JAPAN.prompt: Name the speaker, distinguish his national role from the presidency, and state his assessment of the veto's consequence for the Panel.

CHINA.text: China’s Geng Shuang supported the Panel’s independent work and supported Russia’s proposal for a sanctions time limit and periodic reviews. He explained that China abstained because Russia’s views were not taken on board and consultation time remained.
CHINA.prompt: State China's vote and its explanation. Distinguish its support for the Panel's independent work from its position on the time limit and periodic reviews.

criteria.D1: Identifies the date, United States sponsorship and exact draft symbol.
criteria.D2: States 13–1–1, Russia's veto and China's abstention.
criteria.A1: States the Panel renewal was proposed through 30 April 2025.
criteria.A2: Mentions the proposed midterm and final reports to the 1718 Committee.
criteria.P1: Names Yamazaki, distinguishes his Japanese national statement from the Council presidency, and attributes his assessment that the veto ended Panel operations.
criteria.P2: States China's abstention and reason, its support for independent Panel work, and its support for a sanctions time limit and periodic reviews.
criteria.C1: Preserves the draft's proposal for independent, fact-based assessments.
criteria.C2: Distinguishes the end of the Panel's mandate from the continuation of the Committee and existing sanctions.
criteria.S1: Distinguishes proposed mandate and reporting obligations from actual authority after the vote.
criteria.S2: Separately labels a hypothetical analytical next step without inventing official decisions.

public_reference: On 28 March 2024, U.S. draft S/2024/255 received 13 votes in favour, a Russian veto and a Chinese abstention [VOTE]. The draft proposed extending the 1718 Committee’s Panel of Experts through 30 April 2025, preserving independent, fact-based assessments and requesting midterm and final reports to the Committee [MANDATE, REPORTING]. Neither the extension nor the proposed reporting obligations took effect. The Panel mandate ended on 30 April 2024. The Committee continued and existing sanctions remained in force [SCOPE].
analysis: Analytical suggestion: assess options for continued reporting to the Committee.
critical_errors: Treats the vetoed draft as adopted.
Conflates expiry of the expert Panel with expiration of existing sanctions or the 1718 Committee.
Misattributes a national statement or vote.
